subject: Mach <> Encord
text:
Hi [NAME],

I lead GTM efforts for Physical AI at Encord. We work with a number of
leading UAV and defense focused companies to support their perception stack
as they manage, annotate, and curate multi-sensor data that feeds their
autonomy models.

Many of the customers that we work with partnered with us as the scale of
complexity started to break initial tooling across multi-camera sensor
fusion, large-volume flight data, edge-case mining across diverse
environments. The teams we work with at that stage are usually either
hitting walls with in-house annotation infrastructure or spending
engineering cycles maintaining pipelines that need to be automated.

Would be keen to explore any friction points the Mach team is dealing with
across the data lifecycle and where we can add the most leverage as you're
continuing to scale.

Would love to grab 20 minutes later this week for a quick intro and assess
fit on some of the areas you're focused on.

subject: compounding the IDV loop
text:
Hi [NAME],

I read Meron's post on Sunday and the line: "engineers move ten times
faster, the processes around them don't, PMs become the bottleneck" is very
relevant. The same dynamic applies to the eval layer. When HAL ships IDV
features at that pace, does the adversarial benchmark keep up?

Genuinely curious which side of that you're on.

subject: recommandé par erwan koffi | on travaille avec abbvie, moon surgical, mmi
text:
Bonjour [NAME],

Erwan m'a orienté vers vous côté R&D. On bosse avec des équipes computer
vision médicale comme  Abbvie, Moon Surgical et MMI. En général au moment
où elles scalent l'équipe ML : l'enjeu, c'est de garder les ingénieurs sur
les modèles plutôt que sur la couche data interne, sans rien lâcher sur la
qualité vu que c'est un produit patient.

Plateforme data-centric : curation, annotation 2D/3D, éval modèles et
active learning au même endroit, déployable en VPC.

20 minutes la semaine prochaine pour comparer ?

subject: Label Studio / annotation setup
text:
Hi [NAME],

Had a chat with Uday about [COMPANY]'s ML setup - he mentioned the team is
using Label Studio across chat and voice workflows.

We work with a number of voice AI teams doing similar tasks including the
likes of Sythesia, Udio, Thinking Machine Labs, Gradium and more.

The reason most of them moved off Label Studio is the same i.e. it handles
individual annotation tasks fine but falls apart when you need curation and
annotation in the same place, with QA built in to actually manage
contractor consistency and output quality.

Right now if you're running contractors through Label Studio, my guess is
QA is either manual spot checks or a separate process entirely - does that
sound familiar?

Would love to talk more and see if there is anything Encord could help with
- worth 20-mins next week?

subject: re: automating data curation
text:
Hi[NAME],

I've been speaking with Uday on your team - noticed your profile as someone
driving the automation of data curation and model evaluation internally.

We work with a handful of teams building AI-native contact center products
where the same bottleneck shows up: the pipeline between raw interaction
data and a retrained model has too many manual steps and too many tools.
Annotation in one place, human review in another, eval scoring in a
spreadsheet.

We consolidate that - if it's a pain you're actively trying to solve would
it be worth a call to scope out?

Have time next week Mon, Tues, Thurs?

text:

subject: annotation + eval cost
text:
Hey [NAME],

I spent time going through your multicloud work. Would I be correct in
thinking that the 30% cloud spend reduction also extended to the research
infrastructure?

One problem I've seen that I thought was relevant to your Pulse meeting
launch was the hidden annotation and evaluation cost that wasn't in the
audio roadmap. New ontology, higher QA stakes, it tends to sit on research
engineer time rather than the cloud bill.

The largest IDV company in the space went through the same multimodal
transition on its fraud detection stack. Happy to send the two-pager on
what they did.

Please let me know.

subject: NVIDIA GTC follow-up question
text:
Hi [NAME],

Saw your Nvidia GTC talk and had one questions - as Caper Cart scales to
2,000+ locations, how are you thinking about scaling the annotation
infrastructure for your Shelf Intelligence and Caper Sensors raw data?

The layer between raw sensor inputs and the grocery world model output is
where annotation and curation becomes the critical bottleneck - it's why
teams turn to Encord from tools like Label Studio who cannot handle
multi-camera video and time series data well.

This is because we specialise in that exact area as the data infrastructure
platform purpose-built for CV and physical AI at scale - working with teams
at Boston Dynamics, Physical Intelligence and Woven by Toyota.

Would you be the right person to connect with at Caper, or is there someone
else you'd point me to?
